records.text: A footpad of the Syndicate, a thieves' group led by nobles of fallen Alterac. It strikes at close range with Backstab.
A thief of the Syndicate, a thieves' group led by nobles of fallen Alterac. In a fight, it can use Disarm against an opponent.
A spy of the Syndicate, a thieves' group led by nobles of fallen Alterac. It uses Sneak, strikes with Backstab, and may flee for assistance when badly hurt.
A sentry of the Syndicate, a thieves' group led by nobles of fallen Alterac. It uses Shield Bash in combat.
A saboteur of the Syndicate, a thieves' group led by nobles of fallen Alterac. It uses a ranged shot when fighting.
An assassin of the Syndicate, a thieves' group led by nobles of fallen Alterac. It uses Sneak while out of combat.
An enforcer of the Syndicate, a thieves' group led by nobles of fallen Alterac. It uses Whirlwind in combat.
A mountain yeti encountered in the Alterac region. It uses Frost Breath in combat.
A giant yeti of the Alterac region, larger in name and level than the nearby Mountain Yeti. It uses Frost Breath in combat.
A Crushridge ogre who answers aggression with blunt threats to smash or crush the opponent. The same crude challenge is heard from the other named Crushridge ogre fighters.
A Crushridge brute whose aggro barks match the other named ogre fighters: it threatens to smash or crush its opponent in deliberately rough speech.
A Crushridge mauler, one of the ogres in the force described as Mug'Thol's at Alterac's ruins. Its recorded barks threaten to smash or crush an opponent, and it fights with a Strike.

A Crushridge ogre mage stationed in the Alterac region, this combatant threatens intruders with blunt cries of smashing and crushing. In battle, the mage casts Frostbolt, pairing spellcasting with the warband’s direct aggression.

A Crushridge ogre enforcer in the Alterac region, this combatant answers threats with blunt promises to smash or crush opponents. The enforcer fights at close range, using Head Crack to support the ogres’ forceful assault.

Mug’thol is the leader of the Crushridge ogres who overran the ruins of Alterac, with lieutenants loyal to him. Sent to retrieve the Crown of Will for Lady Sylvanas, he tried it on; the crown let him resist the possession imposed to make him serve her. Melisara describes him as a threat and directs the effort to end his resistance.
Stone Fury is a solitary, powerful stone elemental encountered in the Alterac region. Its combat abilities are Ground Tremor and Trample.
A Dalaran shield guard posted in the Hillsbrad region, this humanoid serves a defensive role. In combat, the guard uses the Violet Shield Effect, consistent with the unit’s shield-bearing duty.
A Dalaran theurgist can cast Frostbolt and Summon Spirit of Old in battle.
A Crushridge warmonger whose combat speech is blunt and aggressive: he boasts of smashing opponents and threatens to kill them.

Baron Vardus is a former noble of Alterac and a high-ranking Syndicate member. Southshore's magistrate describes him as cold-hearted and brutal; the Forsaken want him dead for crimes against them. In combat, he uses Frostbolt and Frost Nova.

Gol'dir says he led an expedition from Durotar under the Warchief's orders and is now a Syndicate captive forced to haul burdens and dig. He reports that Aliden Perenolde planned to enslave his opponents and that Elysa wore a pendant sought by the Warchief. Gol'dir says he will make his own way after settling his business there.
Elysa was kept against her will by Lord Aliden Perenolde. She has Taretha's pendant and gives it up, asking to be left in peace.
An Argus Shadow Mage is an Argus Wake envoy encountered among the Syndicate's strength in the Uplands. In combat, one may threaten to end a fight and cast Shadow Bolt.
A Syndicate wizard casts Frost Armor, even outside combat.

Nagaz is named in a letter as a member of the Argus Wake; the letter's writer says they know nothing of the group beyond its alliance with the Syndicate. A parchment bearing Nagaz's name is magically indecipherable.

Henchman Valik is an injured, dying Syndicate member who expects the enemy to kill him. He offers information for Southshore stout, distrustfully asking whether his visitor's people drink, then shares what he knows after receiving it.

A Dalaran wizard who summons reinforcements and hurls fireballs while defending the ruined outskirts. Magus Voidglare describes the wizards there as patrolling the ruins around their city's magical dome.

An elemental servant of the Dalaran wizards, its rocky body breaking apart as it fights. Magus Voidglare describes the elementals as slaves patrolling the ruined outskirts around the city's magical dome.
A hulking mountain lion, one of the predators in Alterac that Darren Malvew blames for threatening horses near Southshore.
Ricter is a humanoid who flees for help when badly wounded.
Alina is a humanoid combatant who attempts to flee for help when badly wounded.
Dermot is a humanoid combatant who attempts to flee for help when badly wounded.
Kegan Darkmar is a humanoid combatant who attempts to flee for help when badly wounded.
Warden Belamoore is a humanoid spellcaster who uses Fireball, Cone of Cold, and Polymorph in combat. When badly wounded, Belamoore flees for help.
A Crushridge Plunderer is a humanoid attacker who threatens foes with blunt boasts about smashing and crushing, and uses Cleave in combat.
Grel'borg the Miser is an ogre mage rumored to have found the Perenolde Tiara and wander Alterac's ruins seeking more treasure. In battle, Grel'borg uses Bloodlust and Quick Flame Ward.
Targ is one of Mug'Thol's ogre lieutenants, whom Melisara describes as loyal to him. His combat taunts promise to smash or crush an opponent.
Muckrake is one of Mug'Thol's ogre lieutenants. Melisara describes the three as loyal to their leader, though she cannot say what drives that loyalty.
Glommus is one of Mug'Thol's ogre lieutenants, whom Melisara describes as loyal to him. His combat taunts promise to smash or crush an opponent.
Lord Aliden Perenolde is a nobleman targeted by a Horde quest; his manor lies by Lordamere Lake, and Elysa is named as his mistress. In battle he uses shielding and sleep magic.
Jailor Borhuin fights with a net to snare opponents and uses disarming techniques.
The Drunken Footpad is absorbed by Southshore stout, praising it as delicious and playfully singing its praises. His speech reflects a drinker's affection for the local brew.
Narillasanz is dragonkin who uses Flame Breath in combat and Renew when badly wounded.
Skhowl uses Demoralizing Roar and Backhand in combat.
Lo'Grosh uses Bloodlust and Fire Shield III in combat.
Bro'kin sells alchemy supplies.

Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver is a Kirin Tor scholar who wrote a tome on Gurubashi legends and knows the Stone of the Tides. Intrigued by its raw magical potential, he analyzes residue on elemental bracers and proposes disrupting the Stone's amplification with an ancient troll dagger. He found the dagger in Stranglethorn and gave it to his daughter Catelyn, whom he calls willful; she left for Booty Bay to become a pirate.
A Dalaran worker in Hillsbrad Foothills, this level-headed laborer flees for help when badly hurt.
Rizz Loosebolt sells engineering supplies. His shop offers goods for customers to browse.
Nancy Vishas is worried that her husband Sidney has not returned. She thinks work at the Monastery may have delayed him, but senses something is wrong and plans to look outside.

Grandpa Vishas speaks brusquely to Nancy about her missing husband, then defends the Scarlet Crusade's mission to cleanse the world of those he calls impure. His words reveal a hardline zealotry and little concern for her worry.

Bath'rah the Windwatcher has spent ages watching the site where Cyclonian may be summoned, seeking a champion capable of defeating the wind lord. He guides the summoning and says he will use Cyclonian's whirlwind heart to infuse a weapon with its power. His work with elemental spirits and a primal spirit totem also ties him to the forces of nature.

Fahrad is a sardonic, self-assured rogue master who trains rogues and wants challenging locks for them to practice on; he offers throwing knives for Heavy Junkboxes, letting trainees keep some coins. He also recruits promising thieves for Ravenholdt: his letter says they have been watched, calls the recipient's style awkward, and challenges them to find the manor and prove their cunning. He laughs when asked about Milton.

A Ravenholdt Guard of the Assassin's League gathers stolen Syndicate emblems. Jorach says the emblems shame their owners, who are then dealt with within the Syndicate; the guards use theft to weaken a numerous, long-standing enemy.

Lord Jorach Ravenholdt leads the Assassin's League. A small blue bag he considers dear was stolen, and its contents are private. He pursues its recovery and the Azure Key, offering an enchanted garment from his stores to a rogue of exceptional skill and loyalty.
A Ravenholdt Assassin guards the manor with open hostility toward intruders, warning of blades and poison. The manor's security is framed as a lethal threat to those who enter.
Zan Shivsproket is Ravenholdt Manor's speciality engineer and offers goods for browsing.
Smudge Thunderwood is a poison-supplies vendor.
Winstone Wolfe, called The Wolf, is a humanoid.
Simone Cantrell is a landscape architect.
Master Kang is a humanoid.
Carlo Aurelius is an assassin.
Salome is a critter.
Myrokos Silentform speaks of people as pieces in a larger puzzle, guided toward their destination by others who may themselves be guided by a greater force.
Thanthaldis Snowgleam is the Stormpike Supply Officer in Alterac Valley. Thanthaldis offers goods and repairs, and can defend against attackers with cleaves and strikes.
Jekyll Flandring is the Frostwolf Supply Officer in Alterac Valley. Jekyll helps visitors with goods, repairs, and quests, and can fight with a Heroic Strike.

The Abominable Greench is a fearsome creature blamed for stealing Smokywood Pastures' treat shipment and attacking an employee near the yeti grounds in the Alterac Mountains. The victim's account says the Greench left them frozen and describes it wandering nearby. Its recorded cry is a roar.

Sacks works for Smokywood Pastures' Orgrimmar branch and was sent to find a missing package. Encountered as the Strange Snowman, Sacks says an unknown creature attacked him, leaving him very cold. The snowman name describes this encounter; he identifies himself as Sacks.

Corporal Teeka Bloodsnarl is a Horde officer in the Alterac Valley campaign. Her brisk, goading replies challenge recruits who have not assaulted a bunker or captured a mine, asking if they are waiting for others to claim their glory. Her assignments focus on wresting graveyards, defensive positions and mines from the Alliance to advance the Horde war effort.

Sergeant Durgen Stormpike is an Alliance officer in the Alterac Valley campaign. His formal greeting demands a soldier's name, rank and serial number and calls the Frostwolf opposition dirty dogs. He directs soldiers toward enemy graveyards, towers and mines, with an emphasis on securing territory and advancing the Alliance line.

Prospector Stonehewer supports the Stormpike and the Explorers' League's search for artifacts in Alterac Valley. He sees the Frostwolf orcs as an obstacle to scholarly exploration and calls for the defeat of their general, Drek'Thar. Offering treasures to Stormpike heroes, he catches himself saying “plun...” and substitutes “recovered.”

Voggah Deathgrip regards the Stormpike dwarves and their allies as invaders of Alterac Valley and calls for the defeat of their general, Vanndar Stormpike. He takes open pleasure in the prospect of crushing enemies and breaking their lines, and praises such fighters as heroes of the Frostwolf.

Warmaster Laggrond recruits soldiers into the Frostwolf Clan, making recovery of its banner a rite of entry and tracking advancement by rank. He urges defense of Frostwolf and the Warchief, and calls the Winterax a second front, describing Korrak as cruel and cunning. His throat-cutting gesture and demand for Korrak's skull give his orders a blunt edge.

Lieutenant Haggerdin is a Stormpike Guard recruitment officer who tracks soldiers’ standing and handles their rank insignias. He urges the Guard to fight the Frostwolf and celebrates rising heroes; in one reply, he addresses a promoted soldier as commander and says the troops will follow their orders.
Gravis Slipknot is a named humanoid. When reduced to very low health, he tries to flee for assistance.
Araga is a named beast.
Cranky Benj is a beast.
Jimmy the Bleeder is a rare humanoid who flees for help when badly wounded.
Stormpike Battleguards fight for the Stormpike side, using improved blocking and attacking with Rend, Strike, and Charge.
Frostwolf Battleguards fight for the Frostwolf side and use improved blocking in combat.
Mirvyna Jinglepocket represents Smokywood Pastures, offers quests, and sells food and other goods.
Dillord Copperpinch represents Smokywood Pastures, offers quests, and sells food and other goods.

Staffron Lerent is an apothecary of the Royal Apothecary Society who made fragrances intended to leave Alliance and Horde warriors vulnerable to the Shadow Council. He presents the scheme as a way to weaken them through romantic feelings and treats its success as inevitable.
Captain Armando Ossex is a humanoid captain.

Archmage Cedric is a member of the Violet Eye, the Kirin Tor agents watching Karazhan and Medivh. He is wary of Alturus’s disclosure, but uses the report to enlist help: with Karazhan still sealed, he fears the Legion may attack again while the Violet Eye remains powerless. He offers the Violet Eye’s badge as a sign of that responsibility.

Usha Eyegouge is an Alterac Valley battlemaster who resents being left behind to guide others instead of fighting there herself. Her greeting bluntly asks whether a visitor has come to fight the Alliance.
Grumbol Grimhammer is an Alterac Valley battlemaster. He directs visitors toward the fighting, while another response apologizes that they are not experienced enough to survive there.

place_records.text: You are in Alterac Mountains, a highland zone in the Eastern Kingdoms that neither the Alliance nor the Horde holds. The Frostwolf and Stormpike sides fight over Alterac Valley, where officers recruit soldiers for the campaign. Dalaran wizards patrol the ruins of their crater, and Syndicate gangs hold Strahnbrad, where Crushridge ogres and Syndicate spies roam the hollows. Mountain lions prowl the slopes.

You are in Lordamere Internment Camp, a camp in the Alterac Mountains where Alliance guards keep watch. Warden Belamoore, an Alliance spellcaster, is posted here, and transports run from the camp to Menethil Harbor, Theramore, Valiance Keep and Stormwind. Giant moss creepers and elder gray bears roam the camp's edges.

You are in Dalaran Crater, the ruined ground around Dalaran's magical dome in the Alterac Mountains. Dalaran wizards and their elemental servants patrol the outskirts, and Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver, a Kirin Tor scholar, studies the area. Archmage Cedric of the Violet Eye fears the Legion may strike again while Karazhan stays sealed. Giant moss creepers and mountain lions roam the crater, and a mountain yeti is among them.

You are in Strahnbrad, a Syndicate camp in the Alterac Mountains that holds the Horde captive Gol'dir, who is forced to haul burdens and dig. Syndicate spies, wizards and Argus shadow mages patrol the camp, and a jailor named Borhuin watches over the prisoners.

You are in the Ruins of Alterac, a broken town in the Alterac Mountains where a spirit healer offers a return to the living for a price. Bro'kin sells alchemy supplies here. Crushridge fighters and mages, along with giant and mountain yetis, haunt the ruins.
You are in Crushridge Hold, a stronghold of Crushridge ogres and brutes in the Alterac Mountains. Lo'Grosh is among the ogres here.
You are in Slaughter Hollow, a hollow in the Alterac Mountains where Rizz Loosebolt sells engineering supplies from his shop. Crushridge ogres and brutes roam the hollow.

You are in The Uplands, in the Alterac Mountains, where Syndicate sentries and saboteurs watch the ground. Hulking mountain lions and Crushridge ogres roam it, and Grandpa Vishas is among the hostile creatures here.
You are in Lordamere Lake in the Alterac Mountains, where lake frenzies and vile fin tidecallers lurk in the water.
You are in Gallows' Corner in the Alterac Mountains, where Crushridge ogres and brutes roam the ground.

You are in Gavin's Naze, an Alliance post in the Alterac Mountains. Sergeant Durgen Stormpike directs soldiers toward enemy graveyards, towers and mines in Alterac Valley, and Stormpike Battleguards and Captain Armando Ossex stand with him. Mountain lions prowl the outskirts.

You are in Sofera's Naze in the Alterac Mountains, where Henchman Valik, an injured Syndicate member, lies dying and will share what he knows for a mug of Southshore stout. Syndicate footpads and thieves roam the naze, and Jimmy the Bleeder is among the hostile creatures here.
You are in Corrahn's Dagger in the Alterac Mountains, where Syndicate thieves and footpads roam among mountain lions.

You are in The Headland, an Alliance-held spot in the Alterac Mountains. Lieutenant Haggerdin recruits for the Stormpike Guard here and urges the soldiers to fight the Frostwolf orcs. Thanthaldis Snowgleam, the Stormpike supply officer, sells goods and repairs gear, and a prospector of the Explorers' League searches the place for artifacts. Yetis and mountain lions are the dangers around it.

You are in Dandred's Fold, a place that belongs to neither side in the Alterac Mountains. Syndicate assassins and enforcers are the dangers here, along with mountain lions. Elysa, who was kept against her will by Lord Aliden Perenolde, is found here and asks only to be left in peace.

You are in Growless Cave, an Alliance-held cave in the Alterac Mountains. The Alterac Valley battlemaster Grumbol Grimhammer directs visitors toward the fighting, and Stormpike Battleguards stand with him. Giant and mountain yetis are the dangers here.

You are in Chillwind Point, a neutral site in the Alterac Mountains. Bath'rah the Windwatcher has watched for ages the place where the wind lord Cyclonian may be summoned, and he seeks a champion to face him. He says the elemental spirits here no longer favor him. Mountain lions are the dangers around the point.

You are in Ravenholdt Manor, the home of Lord Jorach Ravenholdt, who leads the Assassin's League. Fahrad, a grand master rogue, teaches rogues and recruits promising thieves for the League. Assassins guard the manor with blades and poison, and its vendors sell poisons and other goods.

You are in Alterac Valley, a contested valley in the Alterac Mountains. Alliance and Horde forces fight here for graveyards, towers, bunkers and mines, and the Stormpike and Frostwolf battleguards hold the field for their sides. Usha Eyegouge, the Horde battlemaster, and Grumbol Grimhammer, the Alliance battlemaster, send visitors toward the fighting.
